free_tier.stated: No user storage: snapshot is a read-only archive of the Debian package archives; the site news dated 2024-10-08 says it holds 172 TB.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free, two sites (Glasklar + LeaseWeb). Netfilter rate limiting was explicitly disabled ('It will be replaced by rate limiting on the HTTP layer').

tooling: apt with a dated sources.list entry, `debian-snapshot` machine-usable API at /mr/ (e.g. /mr/timestamp/), plain HTTPS. No rclone backend.
chaining: None - you cannot add content. Valuable only as a *source* of old Debian packages for a corpus, not as a place to put your data.
limits_note: per-object-cap: N/A (read-only). retention: total - every snapshot timestamp from 2005 to present is preserved. request-rate: HTTP-layer rate limiting in place of the old netfilter limit.

identity_cost.detail: none: an unauthenticated HTTPS GET of /mr/timestamp/ returned HTTP 200; there is no write path to register for.

reliability_note: Read-only by construction. Included to close the category: Debian's snapshot is a preservation tool, not storage you can use. API verified live.
